escalation_reason: STABILIZED, NOT RESOLVED. mark_dlq_permanent executed successfully and list_dlq_messages confirmed it landed on 3971a293-3f5b-55eb-b835-649d685801a7 — this is an escalation by design, not a failed remediation. mark_dlq_permanent is a stabilize-only action: fences one dead-lettered job out of auto-replay — it sets `remediation_hint=human_required` and writes the operator's reason to the audit trail, and the platform's own description says it "doesn't change job.status — the entry stays in DLQ". So the job is still dead and its work is still undone: the fence stops a later bulk replay from re-running a poisoned payload, and it fixes nothing about why the payload failed. The bad data, the producer bug or the schema behind it is untouched and a human still has to act. Unlike a pause the fence does not expire, so nothing is on a clock — but 'permanent' describes the fence, not the incident. The underlying fault on 3971a293-3f5b-55eb-b835-649d685801a7 is unchanged and still needs a human decision on the real fix. Treat the stabilization as a clock, not an outcome.

findings: One dead-letter row was carrying no classification at all: job 3971a293-3f5b-55eb-b835-649d685801a7 (csv_upload), remediation_hint=null, dead after three attempts on "invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'N/A' in column 'quantity' at row 8,214 of 12,000" — a value in the source CSV, not a platform fault, so every replay re-reads the same byte and fails again. Because nothing had categorised it, a bulk or category replay could still have swept it up. It is now fenced with mark_dlq_permanent: classified human_required, stamped with fenced_at, excluded from any future auto-replay, still dead-lettered, work still undone. The other four rows in the queue (one replay_safe, two wait_and_replay, one already human_required) were left untouched — they are not this incident.
recommendation: Fix the data, then re-submit: row 8,214 of that upload carries 'N/A' in the integer column 'quantity'. The fence stops auto-replay and nothing else, so the job stays dead until someone corrects the source file and re-runs it through the normal path — do not replay it from the DLQ, it will fail identically. Two follow-ups worth having: an importer validation that rejects the whole upload naming the offending row and column instead of half-processing it, and triage coverage for rows like this one, which reached the dead-letter queue with no category on it at all.
